summary: Settings -> Runtime -> Decoder now has the same in-app ffmpeg installer the first-run wizard uses, plus a server-side file picker for the ffmpeg path. The FFmpeg path field shows a green-tick / red-cross status icon (with a hover/focus balloon tooltip giving the found version+path or why it is missing) and a 'Check' button backed by GET /api/settings/decoder/status. When ffmpeg is not found a 'Download ffmpeg' button runs the background installer (POST /api/settings/decoder/ffmpeg/install, polling /install/status), fills in the installed path, and offers a 'Restart now' button (the wizard restart-and-reload flow) to apply it everywhere. A folder icon inside the input opens a FileBrowserModal backed by a new admin-gated, read-only endpoint GET /api/settings/fs/browse (services.BrowseDirectory) that lists one directory level at a time (directories first, dotfiles hidden, names only -- never file contents). Browsing is sandboxed to a whitelist of roots: the app working directory and its bin/ (where the installer drops ffmpeg), the user's home, and OS-specific common install locations (Windows: C:/ffmpeg[/bin], ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86), ProgramData, LOCALAPPDATA; macOS: /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt/homebrew, /opt/local, /Applications; Linux/other: /usr/bin, /usr/local/bin, /opt, /snap/bin, /bin), plus any extra paths from the new config key decoder.browseRoots. Navigating up stops at a root rather than escaping the sandbox.
compatibility: New optional config key decoder.browseRoots (string array, default empty) adds site-specific picker roots on top of the built-ins. The /api/settings/fs/browse endpoint is admin-only and read-only and only ever returns entry names within the whitelist; a path outside the whitelist (or the default 'ffmpeg' PATH value) falls back to listing the allowed roots. Users can still type any absolute ffmpeg path manually -- the picker is a convenience, and the path is validated by the decoder/installer at use time, not by the browser.
